title: ML Engineer track
summary: Four capstones, ~21 weeks. From building a transformer from scratch through fine-tuning, training stability, and production inference. The capstone bundle that proves you can ship a modern ML system.
contentIntro:
## What this track proves

Four capstones in order:

1. **Build a transformer from scratch** (4-8 weeks) — you understand what every weight does
2. **Fine-tuning + LoRA at scale** (4 weeks) — you can adapt a model to a domain
3. **Training stability at scale** (4 weeks) — you can diagnose + fix real training failures
4. **Inference optimization: KV-cache + quantization** (5 weeks) — you can ship a production inference stack

At the end you have four signed transcripts plus a single track-completion artifact at `/tracks/c/<your-username>-ml-engineer-track`. Hiring managers can verify it themselves with our public key.

*Optional fifth capstone: [RAG pipeline from scratch](/capstones/rag-pipeline-from-scratch). Not required for the track but recommended if you're heading into retrieval territory.*
contentUndergrad:
## What this track proves

The ML Engineer track bundles four capstones into a single ~21-week program. Each capstone produces an independently-signed public artifact (`/capstones/c/<learner>-<capstone>`). Completing all four required capstones auto-mints a track-level completion artifact (`/tracks/c/<learner>-ml-engineer-track`) — a single bundled credential covering the full ramp.

## The four capstones (required, in order)

1. **[Build a transformer from scratch](/capstones/transformer-from-scratch)** — implement a 2-layer transformer in numpy that trains on a copy task. Output: clean understanding of what every weight does, with annotated forward/backward passes.
2. **[Fine-tuning + LoRA at scale](/capstones/fine-tuning-and-lora)** — adapt a base model to a domain dataset using full FT vs LoRA vs QLoRA. Output: an empirical eval table defending each choice.
3. **[Training stability at scale](/capstones/training-stability-at-scale)** — instrument a training run, deliberately break it three ways, and recover from each. Output: a training-discipline toolkit with ablations + scaling-law fit.
4. **[Inference optimization: KV-cache + quantization](/capstones/inference-optimization-kvcache-quant)** — single-GPU inference server, baseline → KV-cache → INT8 → both. Output: tokens-per-second + memory + quality table with production recommendation.

## Optional fifth

- **[RAG pipeline from scratch](/capstones/rag-pipeline-from-scratch)** — six-week retrieval system with eval harness. Strongly recommended if you're heading into retrieval territory.

## Why bundle these specifically

The four required capstones cover the production engineering loop end-to-end: you understand the model (1), can adapt it (2), can stabilize its training (3), and can serve it efficiently (4). Each is a defensible portfolio piece on its own; together they're the ML-engineer ramp-up that B2B teams use to qualify hires.

## Format

21 weeks ranges from a part-time pace (8-10 hours/week) to a full-time bootcamp (4-5 weeks compressed). The track is self-paced — capstone artifacts don't expire. AI tutoring + peer review + the misconception coach run alongside.

Start with capstone #1; the workspace surfaces the next one when you complete each.
contentGrad:
## What this track proves (for someone reading the artifact)

A learner who completes the ML Engineer track has demonstrated:

1. **Mechanistic understanding** — built a transformer from scratch, can defend the role of every layer / weight / activation
2. **Adaptation craft** — empirically compared full fine-tuning, LoRA, and QLoRA on a domain dataset, with controlled ablations
3. **Training-systems discipline** — instrumented a training run, diagnosed three deliberate failure modes from instrumentation alone, fit a scaling-law experiment
4. **Inference-systems judgment** — built a serving stack from baseline through KV-cache + INT8 quantization, made an explicit production recommendation backed by their own measurements

The track-level artifact at `/tracks/c/<learner>-ml-engineer-track` ships with a signed manifest covering all four sub-capstone artifacts; the chain of trust ends at our published ed25519 public key (also signed every individual capstone transcript).

The optional RAG capstone widens the credential to retrieval systems but isn't required for the bundle.

Defense (claim-thread Q&A on the artifact pages) covers each capstone's specific tradeoffs as well as the bundle's overall narrative — why these four together prove production readiness, what they don't prove, what the holes are.
